target_customer: Latin American companies and fintechs that want to launch wallets, cards and payments without building a bank stack
problem: Launching fintech products in Latin America means building from scratch or working with a legacy bank. PayCaddy offers an API with KYC, wallets, payment automation and debit and prepaid card issuing.
business_model: B2B banking as a service API with usage and issuing fees
product_category: banking as a service and card issuing for Latin America

founders.name: Juan Diego Galvez
founders.background_notes: YC page: background in consulting and banking, in electronic payments since 2016.

founders.name: Federico Benavides
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page with no biography; CTO title from a LatamFintech profile.

competitors.name: Pomelo
competitors.what: Argentine fintech as a service platform for card issuing and payments infrastructure across Latin America

technical_complexity.rationale: Standard API engineering over card processors and KYC vendors, with real complexity in regulatory registration and processor integration for several countries.

defensibility.rationale: Registration with the Panama banking supervisor and integrations make it harder to copy than a plain API, though other regional BaaS providers existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Regional BaaS rivals kept growing; Pomelo later raised a $55M Series C in January 2026. No sign that any rival bought PayCaddy.

market_need_then: Latin American fintechs wanted fast card and wallet launches. Pomelo's CEO said a simple prepaid card took 12 to 18 months to launch locally, and PayCaddy pitched speed.

brand_strength.rationale: Regional press and Mastercard recognition as a fintech, but no sourced evidence of brand pull.

outcome_analysis: PayCaddy remains active in Panama as a supervised e-money issuer and says it helps Latin American companies launch cards and wallets. Press from January 2022 followed the YC announcement. Funding is poorly documented: one aggregator lists a $2M seed, and the CEO has said early money came from family offices. Without confirmed rounds it is hard to say whether growth is strong or constrained.
notes: Unverified: a $2.0M seed dated 2022-02 appears only on Seedtable (page blocked on fetch); other aggregators give totals from $0.5M to $4.3M and one lists an October 2024 seed with no amount. The company website only showed a redirect page, so its content was not read. YC page cites Forbes Centroamerica (2022-01-20) and Martes Financiero (2022-01-17) coverage that was not found by search.
